newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, Mexico feature in sugar freight business.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Mexico feature in sugar freight business.

text.p: London's sugar freight market was relatively active on Tuesday, with Brazil and Mexico featuring as quoted origins, shipbrokers said.

Genoc quoted for 14,500 tonnes from Maputo to Portugal for June 23/28 and a further 14,000 tonnes in bags prompt from east coast Mexico to Med/Baltic, Red Sea, Persian Gulf, east Africa and Indian subcontinent.
Shipbrokers said Genoc fixed 16,500/17,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to Kantvik for around June 20 but no rate was given.

Czarnikow Rionda was open for 21/24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic and Jean Lion quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bags from east coast Mexico to Algeria or Iran for prompt shipment.

Fiji Sugar Marketing entered the market with an order for 20,000 tonnes in bulk from Fiji to London for July 1/10 and CSR was open for 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to US Gulf/Atlantic for the same dates.

Of the day's other firmer business, shipbrokers said Sucre Export fixed 13/13,500 tonnes in bags from south China to Pakistan/Red Sea for prompt dates and Andre 4,000 tonnes from Santos to Banjul, also for prompt.
Amerop fixed two bulk sugar orders to US Gulf/Atlantic for the second half of June -- 15,000 tonnes from Barahona, completing Rio Haina, and a further 15,500 tonnes from Salaverry.

Elsewhere, Bangladesh bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar for June/July shipment from a Saudi firm and Iraq was reported to have bought 12,500 tonnes of Brazilian whites under the U.N.-sponsored oil-for-food programme.
